_comment: Shared MCP_FS_SANDBOX_MAX_BYTES parity table for the filesystem-sandbox dual port (#137). Lives at the repo root, not under servers/, because it is not a server -- tools/check-architecture-doc.mjs requires every servers/ entry to be a documented server.
Both test suites read THIS file, so the two ports are exercised against literally the
same inputs and expectations rather than two hand-maintained copies that can drift.
#98 unified the grammar (which literal forms parse). It did not unify the value domain,
which is why every row carries an expected `max_bytes` and not just accept/reject:
TS silently rounded 9007199254740993 down to ...992 while Python applied it exactly,
and a 310-digit value overflowed to Infinity in TS (server refuses to start) while
Python accepted an effectively unbounded cap. Asserting only accept/reject would have
let the rounding row pass on the broken tree.
`raw` values longer than a literal are expressed as {"digits": N} = '1' followed by N-1 zeros.
